blocks.text: The first theme is about whom the Western Cape sells to, when and how. It holds three focus areas: the segments, the green season and the bookability of the province. Together they decide whether interest becomes a trip: the right travellers, in months with room and on product they can book.

Country is too blunt a target for a long-haul destination. Within one market, travellers differ in what they want from a trip, what they spend and where they book. Four values-based segments fit the Western Cape. Together they hold about 97 million addressable travellers, and each is concentrated in named home markets (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p41 to p43). Marketing to a segment inside a market puts each rand where the province is most likely to win.

The prize to 2035 is value as much as volume. Curious Explorers and Creative Connectors together hold over 40% of global outbound leisure demand, while Discerning Connoisseurs deliver the highest economic impact per arrival (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Strategic Implications"). The segments also help with season and spread. Curious Explorers offer the strongest opportunity for dispersal beyond Cape Town, and Reflective Adventurers support seasonality mitigation through year-round outdoor and wellness travel (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p56).

The measure holds the province back as much as the message. Performance is judged on arrivals. The Department of Economic Development says current growth framing "overemphasises visitor volumes" and that a value and spend lens may suit better (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p24).

The four segments rest on a May 2025 survey of more than 25,000 outbound travellers in 34 markets, applied to 17 priority markets (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Research Methodology"). Each segment has its own home markets, spend and booking channels, so one campaign cannot reach all four. China holds the largest pool, about 21.49 million, but air access and visas constrain its conversion (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Comparative Market Potential Overview").

Yet two limits apply. The survey leaves out the domestic market and seven African markets, among them Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Research Methodology"). Its findings are directional rather than definitive, and no Western Cape validation exists yet (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Disclaimer"). Stakeholders also name interests outside the four: medical tourism, township culture, eco-adventure and international MICE (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p34, p35, p42, p45). These are product interests that cut across the segments, not a fifth segment.

Wesgro should market by segment within market and judge results by value as well as volume. The UK and Germany anchor the near term with a combined pool of about 12.5 million, and the USA is the largest single pool outside China (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Strategic Implications"). The same research that tests the segments here should extend them to the domestic and African markets, which the survey leaves out.

The order matters. Segment targets and validation come first, in 2027. The findings are directional, and the budget should not move on them at scale until they hold for the Western Cape (section 4.3). Spend moves to each segment's own channels from 2028. Spend per visitor joins Wesgro's targets from 2029, once the data exists to track it.

Segment targeting works because it moves money to where incidence, fit and channel meet. Curious Explorers are 30% of UK and US travellers, and the province scores 4.6 out of 5 on its ability to win them (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Segment Incidence by Market", "Ability-to-Win Assessment"). Discerning Connoisseurs book 42% of trips through luxury travel advisors and 6% through OTAs (Skift Segmentation Analysis, Mar 2026, "Travel Behaviour and Spend"). Broad awareness misses them, while advisor partnerships reach them at the point of sale.

New Zealand gives each priority market a role, with the USA as its high-yield growth engine (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p53). It judges performance on revenue per visitor and length of stay over arrivals (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p55). Valencia matches product to purpose in a similar way, with sector-led programmes from gastronomy to business events that attract purpose-driven, higher-value travellers (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p48). Its tourist spend rose 21% in 2024 and spending per trip 6.3%, though no source isolates the programmes' share of that rise (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p46). The transfer depends on two changes: yield metrics beside the arrivals count, and partnerships with specialist distribution networks (Global Benchmarking Report, Mar 2026, p56).

**Initiative I1**, segment-led activation and yield in mature markets, carries this entry with focus area 5 (section 4.3). **Indicators** T1-01 international arrivals, T1-02 arrivals by market group and T1-03 direct foreign spend at impact level, and T2-01 segment home-market arrivals at outcome level (section 5.2).
